title: The right hand panel has one settled rule for what you see when you pick something
goal: You already answered how this should work: what you picked sits at the top. The settings for the thing you just clicked belong at the top of the right hand panel, directly under the layers list, with Appearance and Effects following under them, and a plain shape moves nothing because it has no section of its own. Today three separate mechanisms fight over that job: the order the sections sit in, the panel scrolling itself to whatever you just picked, and the room the Effects list keeps for the effect you just opened. Each was built on its own, so picking text can leave its settings off the bottom, picking a plain rectangle can leave the panel parked where the last pick left it, adding an effect can leave every one of its settings below the cut, and picking a row can scroll the layers list itself off the top. Make the three one rule, write it down, and let the panel follow it.
notes:

What fixed it: 7f65ae4d, Picking a layer brings its own section into view, audit queue/audits/2026-09-09-dock-picked-first-reveal.json. The panel now scrolls itself to the picked section. That is option scroll on this task's own decision card, shipped by a neighbouring task while the card was still pending, and unflagged. So the question was answered by the app rather than by the user.

Why the card still stands. The shipped scroll has a cost the audit names itself: the panel holds about 1030 points of sections in a 690 point window, so showing the Text section means the layers list goes off the top. You click a row and the list of rows leaves. Picking from the layers list is the main way anybody moves between layers while building UI, so a click that takes the list away is worth an answer rather than a default.

It also crosses a written rule. UX-PATTERNS section 3, Reveal: ambient changes never may, a selection moving, a document loading, a background update leave a shut header shut and do not scroll. A selection moving now scrolls the dock. Either the rule moves or the behaviour does; that scrub is filed separately.

Folded in from two-panel-walks-are-failing-on-main, closed as done by the same pass: panel-controls-walk was fixed by 64ac9f3c, and a verified alternative to the scroll is in hand there, a v5 order migration moving the picked section above Effects, guarded by shapePartsEnabled, which makes the walk pass at 1200x720 with no self-scrolling at all.
acceptance: The answered rule is written into the dock rules in UX-PATTERNS and the code follows it: what you picked sits at the top, under the layers list, with Appearance and Effects under that
Picking a piece of text shows the whole Text section without anybody scrolling, on a 1200 by 720 window
Picking a plain rectangle straight after picking text leaves the panel showing a section that starts with its own heading, not a cut-off colour row
Adding an effect leaves that effect settings on screen, not below the bottom edge of the Effects list
Clicking a row in the layers list does not scroll that list off the top, so the next row you want is still under your hand
The height sharing arithmetic and the scroll-to-what-you-picked routines come out of the dock view into a file of their own, since all three are being rewritten anyway
All four panel walks pass on their own and in a sweep: dock-picked-first-walk, layers-list-follows-pick-walk, effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk, panel-start-margin-walk

log.note: REPRODUCED on a fresh probe build of clean main. `Scripts/playtest-all.sh dock-picked-first` -> dock-picked-first-walk 16s FAILED step 47 (waitFor): sectionInView("Text") did not happen within 4.0s. The dock's own offsets in a 688pt viewport: text picked -> Text 602-778 (dockInView stops at Measurements); measurement picked -> Measurement 502-781; zoom callout right after it is drawn -> Zoom Callout 627-741; plain rectangle -> Appearance 169-431, whole. A second run with the waitFor steps stripped out also failed on `press Details`, because the Measurement section's Details control is itself off the window. Same bug, second symptom.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of the three directions, before building any of them. (a) auto-scroll: fine when you pick on the canvas, bad when you pick in the layers list, which is where the walk picks and where half of real picking happens. Bringing Text whole into view costs 90pt of travel, which takes the Layers header off the top and leaves about a row and a half of the list under the pointer that just clicked it. Motion on every selection, for a problem the order can solve without any motion. (b) picked section first: arithmetic on the measured heights puts Text at 169-345 and Appearance at 345-546 both whole, Effects 546-691 (3pt cut), Measurement at 169-448 whole, callout 169-283 whole, and a plain rectangle unchanged, so the 2026-09-07 arrangement survives untouched in the case it was asked for. Shortest change too: one more numbered migration in loadOrder moving pickedSections before .color instead of before .geometry. (c) auto-fold: the app has to guess what you are not using and will guess wrong (a shadow on a label needs Effects open while text is picked), and it overwrites collapse state the user set by hand. Rejected. The note's worry that a measurement still would not fit under (b) is out of date: the Details fold brought that section from 470pt to 279pt, so it fits at 169-448.

Decision filed with the numbers and a real screenshot of the panel with text picked: queue/decisions/picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t-when-you-pick-something-on-the-c.{json,md} plus 2026-09-08-picked-below-the-fold-today.png.
